concepts.name: observatory
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / stylized-concept.
Create a finished art-direction review sheet for the iOS game Starfall, a substantial redesign of the Moonlit Observatory. Landscape 1536x1024 sheet with two views: phone portrait on the left (about 35% sheet), iPad landscape on the right (about 65%). No device bezels. Small headings outside the art: "OBSERVATORY • CONCEPT", "Phone", "iPad". Label footer "Concept illustration — not a native capture".
Use reference 1 ONLY for the world's original feeling: an actual moonlit mountain observatory, weathered violet stone, warm brass, flowering crevices, cloud chasms, stairs, towers and a blue moon. Use reference 2 for the CURRENT six faceted crystal star characters. Use reference 3 ONLY to understand actual seven-column by seven-row gameplay and control semantics; its disconnected props and giant rectangular slab are the problem to FIX.
The game takes place on a convincing continuous piece of cliffside architecture seen from a steep overhead isometric-like camera. Build a clearly defined playable terrace into a MUCH LARGER scene. Foreground masonry has thickness and irregular buttresses; stairs visibly reach the terrace; rear paths lead to an observatory tower. A large brass telescope bolts to a raised octagonal pedestal joined by visible stairs to the SAME rock/terrace. A lantern rests on a connected stone shoulder with a visible base and warm contact pool. No floating cutout props. Consistent perspective and scale everywhere. Detailed story-rich scenery surrounds a calm dark blue-violet landing surface. Architecturally believable contact shadows and low warm grazing light, cyan moon rim. Keep foreground readable, not muddy.
Critical mapping: the playable floor has exactly SEVEN straight near-horizontal rows and SEVEN columns of positions, gentle taper only, high camera. No diamond board, no floor cell grid, no circle under ordinary stars. Show roughly 22 CURRENT crystal stars occupying the lower four of seven rows, empty upper rows; distinct aqua tall four-point, amber five-point, mint six-point, pink eight-ray, violet wide four-point, one dark violet star. Preserve crystal faces and proportions. Small physical contact shadows. A narrow brass inlay follows the exact outer playable boundary, separated from scenery. Stars remain the visual focus.
Top score and menu belong INSIDE a shallow dark groove CUT INTO a low rear parapet. The stone extends around and behind the recess; bevels, occlusion and mounting make it physical. Render clean ivory native-looking "24" with small golden sparkle at left and a simple small constellation menu icon at right. No app cards.
Bottom dialogue is a broad hollow carved into the FRONT terrace ledge on phone; on iPad it is a connected side alcove reached by masonry, with its own supporting wall and same light. Show a small Spark portrait mounted within the hollow and exact short readable text: "Spark" and "A little room for the next shower." Native-looking actions "Resume sky" and "Next shower" engraved/light-inlaid within the quiet dark surface. It is part of the terrain with continuous connected edges, not a rectangular UI overlay. Keep generous readable text and visible button recesses.
Phone: board dominant, but rear scenery and front stairway visible; narrower telescope shoulder without invading play. iPad: board is NOT stretched across the screen; expand terrain, tower base, bridges and garden along sides, with dialogue in the connected right alcove. Render scene to frame edges, no generic wallpaper collage or blur. Convey interaction through a small warm lantern response and telescope lens glint, no circles/arrows around controls. A coherent polished game scene, rich detail, no repeated empty slabs.

concepts.name: prism-tide
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / stylized-concept.
Create a polished game-environment art direction sheet for Starfall: "PRISM TIDE • CONCEPT". A CONTRAST to the grounded moonstone Observatory. Landscape 1536x1024 review sheet with phone portrait view on the left (about 35%) and iPad landscape on the right (about 65%), small headings "Phone" and "iPad", no device bezels. Footer "Concept illustration — not a native capture".
Use the attached CURRENT Crystal Glow cast reference for the exact character vocabulary: tall aqua four-point, amber five-point, mint six-point, pink eight-ray, wide violet four-point, dark violet five-point crystal stars with large blue eyes.
Build a luminous transparent crystal VESSEL suspended within a deep twilight grotto/galaxy sea: an organic tall open-topped glass basin with a calm midnight-blue translucent play volume inside, thick refracting opal lips and clear layered walls. It is a volumetric object with an optically convincing near wall, rounded machined crystal cut edges, caustic light and faint cyan-violet-prism dispersion. Tiny galaxy light is INSIDE the thick glass, kept peripheral and dark behind stars. This is Liquid Glass-like MATERIAL inspiration, never generic glass UI cards. No rectangular slab, no stone game frame. Vessel has a distinctive flowing asymmetrical outer silhouette; the actual playable interior is a quiet gently tapered rectangular seven-by-seven field with a continuous thin luminous boundary. Keep distortion OUTSIDE the playable interior. High overhead three-quarter camera, upright stars retain proportions and contrast. Show EXACTLY SEVEN columns of possible star positions, seven potential rows, only lower four rows partly occupied by about 24 current cast stars, with empty upper space for showers. No square floor backgrounds, no circles around ordinary stars. Subtle local reflections and depth make stars occupy the inner landing membrane rather than float unrelated to it.
The upper controls are physically sculpted INTO the thick rear rim of the vessel: one dark, optically quiet carved channel showing golden sparkle "24" and small constellation menu icon in crisp pale native-looking type. Actual glass continues behind and around the groove.
The bottom communication space is a hollow scooped INTO the thick lower glass lip, with a dark matte/refractive readable interior. Small Spark portrait, exact readable text "Spark" and "A little room for the next shower." Buttons "Resume sky" and "Next shower" sit within that physical lip. On iPad the vessel flows into a connected lateral hollow, with visible continuous glass walls connecting it to the main vessel. No disembodied rectangles or UI overlays.
Two independently interactive objects are visibly connected to the vessel OUTSIDE the arena: a shell-shaped fountain built into a rear crystal spout, and a luminous pearl set in a three-prong opal socket on the lower rim. Show unambiguous mounting, material continuity, contact occlusion, consistent scale/light/perspective. A fountain tap sends a small visible ripple down its channel and a pearl tap brightens the refracted light in the surrounding lip, without new controls.
Phone: full-screen scene, large usable play interior and clearly separated readable hollows, surrounding dark lagoon and floating crystal formations visible around the silhouette.
iPad: retain star/board scale, extend grotto scenery and translucent vessel depth to sides, show nebula and reflected light through glass edges. Beautiful precise high-end stylized game art, moonlit indigo/cyan with restrained prismatic highlights and amber character accents. Stars brighter than scenery; thick believable optical glass, not foggy plastic.
concepts.refinement: Refine this concept sheet only. Preserve both phone and iPad compositions, all typography, exact star character shapes and faces, vessel silhouette, built-in control/message hollows, grounded shell fountain and pearl socket. Remove EVERY grid line and every regularly spaced tiny star/node from the interior play surface. The inside must be a QUIET open midnight-blue translucent volume without a cell grid or circles. Reduce the luminosity and multicolored glitter of the glass rims by about 40%, retaining clear transparent thickness, localized optical highlights and subtle prism edges. The actual character stars must have the strongest contrast. Do not add anything else. Keep footer identifying it as concept, not native capture.
